body.statement: Under complete randomization, \(\mathbb E W_1(\widehat F_a,F_a)\le\tfrac12\sqrt{\rho_a}\) and \(W_1(G_a,\widehat F_a)\le N^{-1}\). For the quantile-lifted triple \(G\), \(|L_N(G)-L_N(F)|\le D_N(F,G)/(N-1)\) and \(\max\{|U_{\mathrm{lo}}(G)-U_N(F)|,|U_{\mathrm{hi}}(G)-U_N(F)|\}\le[D_N(F,G)+3456/N]/(N-1)\), with \(\mathbb ED_N(F,G)\le M_N\). If \(n_a/N\to p_a\in(0,1)\), all three endpoint estimates have error \(O_{\mathbb P}(N^{-3/2})+O(N^{-2})\). For every \(\eta\in(0,1)\), the computable interval \([U_{\mathrm{lo}}(G)-[M_N/\eta+3456/N]/(N-1),U_{\mathrm{hi}}(G)+[M_N/\eta+3456/N]/(N-1)]\) covers \(U_N(F)\) with probability at least \(1-\eta\).
body.justification: The sampling result separates armwise observation error from the smaller deterministic realization error and remains valid at ties and nonunique transport optima.
body.gap: Aronow, Green, and Lee (2014) establish consistent two-arm sharp-bound estimators, and Gao, Ge, and Qian (2025) analyze superpopulation fractional plug-ins; neither treats a three-arm realizable endpoint under dependent sampling without replacement.
body.consumer: The result gives a conservative finite-sample uncertainty band for the sharp variance endpoint when no experiment reveals all three population marginals.
body.proof_tex:
For a distribution \(H\) on \([0,1]\), use its nondecreasing quantile \(Q_H\).  The one-dimensional transport identity
\[
 W_1(H,K)=\int_0^1|Q_H(u)-Q_K(u)|\,du
 =\int_0^1|H(t)-K(t)|\,dt
\]
follows for finite laws by matching equal infinitesimal quantile masses and applying \(|r-s|=\int_0^1|\mathbf1\{r\le t\}-\mathbf1\{s\le t\}|\,dt\).  On the interval \(((j-1)/N,j/N]\), monotonicity bounds the integral error from its midpoint value by \(N^{-1}\) times the quantile variation on that interval.  These variations telescope to at most one, so def:plugin-lift gives
\[
 W_1(G_a,\widehat F_a)\le N^{-1}.
\]

Under ass:complete-randomization, arm \(a\) reveals a simple random sample without replacement of size \(n_a\) from the fixed column.  At every \(t\in[0,1]\), the variable \(n_a\widehat F_a(t)\) is hypergeometric.  Direct indicator covariance calculation gives
\[
 \mathbb E\widehat F_a(t)=F_a(t),\qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(\widehat F_a(t))
 =\rho_aF_a(t)\{1-F_a(t)\},
 \quad \rho_a=\frac{N-n_a}{n_a(N-1)}.
\]
Tonelli's identity above and Cauchy--Schwarz therefore imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E W_1(\widehat F_a,F_a)
 &=\int_0^1\mathbb E|\widehat F_a(t)-F_a(t)|\,dt\\
 &\le\sqrt{\rho_a}\int_0^1\sqrt{F_a(t)\{1-F_a(t)\}}\,dt
 \le\frac12\sqrt{\rho_a}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The triangle inequality yields \(\mathbb EW_1(G_a,F_a)\le\tfrac12\sqrt{\rho_a}+N^{-1}\).  This calculation is armwise and uses no independence between arms.

We next prove the deterministic perturbation bounds.  If \(X_a,Y_a\in[0,1]\), then both contrasts lie in \([-1/2,1/2]\), whence
\[
 \left|\left(\sum_ac_aX_a\right)^2-
 \left(\sum_ac_aY_a\right)^2\right|
 \le\sum_a|c_a|\,|X_a-Y_a|.
\]
Glue coordinatewise optimal \(W_1\) transports to any coupling of \(F\), conditionally and independently given its coordinates.  The resulting triple has marginals \(G\).  Applying the displayed inequality and then reversing \(F,G\) proves
\[
 |V_{\mathrm{rel}}(F)-V_{\mathrm{rel}}(G)|
 \le\sum_a|c_a|W_1(F_a,G_a).
\]
The same argument with suprema proves this bound for \(C_{\max}\).  When both triples have \(N\) equally weighted occurrences, the sorted coordinatewise matching realizes each \(W_1\); applying its three bijections to an optimal schedule and reversing the roles proves
\[
 |V_{\mathrm{int}}(F)-V_{\mathrm{int}}(G)|
 \le\sum_a|c_a|W_1(F_a,G_a).
\]

Also
\[
 |\mu_a(F)-\mu_a(G)|\le W_1(F_a,G_a).
\]
Since \(v_a(H)=\min_{m\in[0,1]}\int(x-m)^2\,dH(x)\) and \(x\mapsto(x-m)^2\) is uniformly \(2\)-Lipschitz, comparison at the two minimizing means gives
\[
 |v_a(F)-v_a(G)|\le2W_1(F_a,G_a).
\]
Moreover \(|\theta_N(F)|,|\theta_N(G)|\le1/2\), so
\[
 |\theta_N(F)^2-\theta_N(G)^2|
 \le|\theta_N(F)-\theta_N(G)|
 \le\sum_a|c_a|W_1(F_a,G_a).
\]
Combining the last three displays with the definitions of \(B_N,D_N\) and the cost perturbation bounds gives
\[
 |L_N(G)-L_N(F)|\le\frac{D_N(F,G)}{N-1},\qquad
 |U_N(G)-U_N(F)|\le\frac{D_N(F,G)}{N-1}.
\]
Taking expectations in the definition of \(D_N\) gives \(\mathbb ED_N(F,G)\le M_N\).

Apply thm:variance-certificate to \(G\).  Its deterministic rounding width implies
\[
 0\le U_N(G)-U_{\mathrm{lo}}(G)\le\frac{3456}{N(N-1)},
 \qquad
 0\le U_{\mathrm{hi}}(G)-U_N(G)\le\frac{3456}{N(N-1)}.
\]
The triangle inequality therefore proves
\[
 \max\{|U_{\mathrm{lo}}(G)-U_N(F)|,
 |U_{\mathrm{hi}}(G)-U_N(F)|\}
 \le\frac{D_N(F,G)+3456/N}{N-1}.
\]

If \(n_a/N\to p_a\in(0,1)\), then \(\rho_a=O(N^{-1})\), the coefficients in \(D_N\) are bounded, and \(\mathbb ED_N=O(N^{-1/2})+O(N^{-1})\).  Markov's inequality gives \(D_N=O_{\mathbb P}(N^{-1/2})+O(N^{-1})\).  Division by \(N-1\), together with the deterministic rounding term, proves the claimed \(O_{\mathbb P}(N^{-3/2})+O(N^{-2})\) errors for \(L_N(G),U_{\mathrm{lo}}(G),U_{\mathrm{hi}}(G)\).

Finally, for \(\eta\in(0,1)\), Markov's inequality and \(\mathbb ED_N\le M_N\) give
\[
 \mathbb P\{D_N(F,G)\le M_N/\eta\}\ge1-\eta.
\]
On this event the preceding bounds place \(U_N(F)\) inside
\[
 \left[U_{\mathrm{lo}}(G)-\frac{M_N/\eta+3456/N}{N-1},
 U_{\mathrm{hi}}(G)+\frac{M_N/\eta+3456/N}{N-1}\right].
\]
All endpoints and radii in this display are computable from the observed arm samples, the known design sizes, the fractional program, and the deterministic rounding output.
